number.why: The source explicitly reports ovulation in 9/12 metformin participants and 4/15 placebo participants. These counts yield a reconstructed OR of 8.25; the OR and a confidence interval are not published in the held texts. Confirmation applies to the reported counts, not to the served 'as randomised' label, which remains unestablished as the ruling acknowledges. Follow-up ends at protocol-defined stopping criteria rather than a fixed duration.

quotes.span: In the metformin and placebo groups, 9 of 12 participants (75%) and 4 of 15 participants (27%) ovulated, and 6 of 11 participants (55%) and 1 of 14 participants (7%) conceived, respectively.
Serum P level > or =4 ng/mL was considered to indicate ovulation.
Patients completed the study when they had had six ovulatory cycles, became pregnant, or experienced anovulation while receiving 150 mg of CC.

entry.why: The source establishes a randomized placebo-controlled trial in anovulatory women with PCOS resistant to clomiphene, with clomiphene subsequently administered alongside both assigned treatments. This fits the question; prior clomiphene resistance is not an exclusion in that question.

quotes.span: PATIENT(S): Anovulatory women with the polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) who were resistant to CC.
Participants received placebo or metformin, 500 mg three times daily, for 7 weeks.
Metformin or placebo was continued and CC treatment was begun at 50 mg daily for 5 days.

missed: No additional finding changes either verdict. The numerical confirmation must retain the ruling's analysis-population limitation and distinguish the reconstructed OR from the explicitly reported arm counts.
